summary_of_work: Read THREAT_MODEL.md, AUDIT.md, the context file, and the rejection paths of machine.cpp (collect_mcycle_root_hashes, collect_mcycle_bundle, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, append_uarch_reset_root_hash, append_revert_uarch_tail_period, collect_uarch_cycle_bundle, check_cmio_response_revert_root_hash, log/verify of send_cmio_response, step and reset), send-cmio-response.cpp, uarch-reset-state.cpp and the record/replay revert_state, interpret.cpp break-reason precedence, doc/recipes/prt.lua (mcycle and uarch builders, begin_input tail capture, run_to_input_mcycle_offset revert, forked and stored pairs and their revert, machine caches, collect_mcycle_bundle/collect_uarch_cycle_bundle/prove_state_transition, stored epoch state with pad_bundle rebuild and reopen/revert_interrupted_input, validate_state_transition_response), vg.lua's rejection handling, the CLI's mcycle and uarch computation-hash builders, Dave's CartesiStateTransition, and libcmt/rollup CLI/rollup-http-server reject paths (machine-guest-tools v0.18.1-test1). I built a scripted bare-metal guest (scratch guest/g.c: emit output, emit report, dirty pages, spin, spin until a given mcycle, reject, accept, exception, halt) and ran five differential experiments. exp1: for 7 scenarios (immediate rejection of the first input, rejection after emitting an output and a report, rejection after dirtying pages, rejection after earlier accepts, oversized input, exception, halt), it reran the uarch step by step with run_uarch and reset_uarch, substituting the revert hash when rejected, and compared that reference with collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes at bundle sizes 0,1,3,10,19,20 from 4 start points around the rejection (before, in the rejecting mcycle, at the rejected fixed point, after it), with collect_uarch_cycle_bundle at offsets 0,1,n-2,n-1 for bundles 0,3,20, and with logged and verified uarch steps plus a reset. ALL OK. exp2: delivery at mcycle 2^64-100000 with imcyclemax saturated, and a rejection landing exactly at imcyclemax=UINT64_MAX. Checked the mcycle collection at bundles 0-4, the uarch collection with the revert tail, the uarch bundle, the logged steps and the reset (reset verify gives the revert hash), and a delivery to the canonical state. All consistent. exp3: on the EVM harness (regenerated step, shared anvil not restarted), ran every uarch step of the rejecting mcycle, stepThenReset at the rejecting mcycle (returns the revert hash), the following mcycle from the canonical state, and delivery+step of the next input, for three scenarios including two rejections in a row and outputs and reports before the rejection. ALL OK. exp4: ran the PRT player from doc/recipes/prt.lua as a forked player and as a stored player closed and reopened after every input and after the seal, on inputs R, o, opwR, R, o, sR (the first input, two in a row and the last input of the epoch rejected). The two mcycle claims were equal and their final leaf was canonical. Leaf proofs at periods before, at and after each rejection matched the reference. Uarch claims for the rejecting period and the next one were equal between the two players, and their last leaf equalled the mcycle leaf. prove_state_transition at 6-9 positions per claim verified from the agreed leaf to the claimed leaf: before the rejecting mcycle, in it, at its reset, in the next mcycle and in the later period. The delivery transition of the input that follows each rejection verified too. ALL OK. exp5 and the CLI: cartesi-machine --mcycle-computation-hash with bundle 4 gave the same root as the player (0x108eb9f6...). --uarch-cycle-computation-hash for the rejecting periods of inputs 0 and 2 gave the same root at bundles 0 and 19 as the player's uarch claims (0x49d61064..., 0x60197195...). No disagreement was found, so no candidate is reported.
not_covered: Dave's deployed CartesiStateTransition and Tournament on the local chain: the rejection paths were checked through the harness StepVerifier wrapper over the same regenerated libraries (stepThenReset, step, sendCmioResponseThenStep) and by reading CartesiStateTransition. No transitionState call with InputBox inputs through a deployed DaveConsensus provider, and no full tournament that settles a rejected last input on chain.

End-to-end PRT runs with the referee model or the chain bridge (prt-demo, player-restart runner) using a rejecting guest. The player was driven by direct event-handler calls without the transport, bridge, or crisium.

Crash or kill of the stored player at points inside a rejected input (between pair:revert's remove_stored and clone_stored, and between revert and commit_epoch_state). Only clean close and reopen at input boundaries and after the seal were exercised.
The stored player's agreed pair (advance_agreed_pair, agreed.revert) across a rejected input. It only runs during a bisection, which the direct-call experiment did not drive.
A rejection at imcyclemax with an unsaturated imcyclemax (2^48 mcycles after delivery). This was argued from the code, which is the same as the saturated case that was tested.

Linux and guest-tools guests (libcmt cmt_rollup_finish reject, the rollup CLI, rollup-http-server /finish reject) were read, not run. A rejection with cached hash-tree state of large Linux machines, timer interrupts or TLB-heavy rejecting mcycles was not exercised. Only bare-metal guests were used.
Sampling periods other than 2^10 (for example Dave's released 2^18) for the player's claims around rejections, and mcycle bundle sizes other than 0-4 (emulator) and 4 (player).

JSON-RPC (forked player) versus local differences were covered only through the forked player's own calls. remote fork_server, swap and rebind failures during machine_pair:revert were not fault-injected.
ZK step logs (log_step/verify_step) on rejecting machines: out of scope.
Inspect-state requests interleaved with rejections (outside the verified history).
